answer: Continuous dilution fee. Each identity pays a fee that rises with the square of identities registered under one registrant, so a whisper of extra accounts costs little but a knoll of ten thousand pays steeply. Registrants must post shale-denominated collateral covering projected fees; fees are deducted continuously. An attacker sustaining N sybils pays roughly c·N² per period, making mass duplication capital-destroying rather than merely costly.
